answer: Agents stake reputation on a tiered ledger where each terrace of trust unlocks greater voting weight, so a fresh identity forged at the lowest terrace earns almost nothing. A kernel rule enforces a long lockup horizon before any new identity gains influence, making rewards accrue slower than costs. The attacker's bottleneck: creating thousands of shells costs real stake held across that full horizon, while each shell's payout stays flat, so sybil spam bleeds capital instead of compounding power.
